TextView.android:text: Receive authentication requests while using other apps or with the screen locked. Navi keeps a quiet computer-connection notification while its listener runs. Each approval still needs your fingerprint.

Allow notifications for Navi. Keep Computer connection enabled for the persistent service notification; it can stay Silent. Set Authentication requests to Alerting, with sound or vibration and Pop on screen if offered.

Tap below and choose Allow in Android’s battery-optimization prompt. The listener needs network access during sleep to deliver requests promptly. This can use more battery. Navi waits for incoming connections; it does not hold the screen on.

On Pixel, also check App battery usage: allow background usage and choose Unrestricted if offered. Turn off Pause app activity if unused (or Manage app if unused). Other phones may have an Auto-start permission or Sleeping apps list: allow Navi to auto-start and exclude it from sleeping apps. These names vary by Android version.

Return to Navi and tap Enable network authentication. Approve the one-time fingerprint prompt if requested. Wait for Ready on your network. Your paired computer can then send requests over the same reachable Wi-Fi/LAN. You can press Home, swipe away the app’s recent task, and lock the screen.

Navi remembers your choice and restarts after an app update or after reboot and the first phone unlock. Keep Wi-Fi connected. Opening Navi also resumes an enabled listener. Turn off network authentication in Navi to stop it and disable automatic restart.

Check for Navi · computer authentication in the notification shade. Android 14 and newer may let you swipe away even an ongoing notification; that does not stop the listener. Reopen Navi to restore its notification. If you use Force stop or Android’s Active apps → Stop control, open Navi again to resume.

Reserve the phone’s IP in your router if your computer uses a fixed address. Guest Wi-Fi or client isolation can block direct connections. After setup, test once with the screen locked and again after reboot and first unlock. Battery Saver, vendor restrictions, or a lost connection can still delay delivery; no app can promise uninterrupted availability.
